chapter_title: Concerning the Fasting of the Saints
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶3:** The first spiritual
 labor
 is
 this
: When
 one
 who
 is being regenerated disciplines
 the
 external natural man by
 with
holding from the desires of self-
love and the senses, he brings
 into
 subjection the entire
 dominion of the proprium — the
 self
-will that
 rules
 within
 him.

**¶4:**
 The
 second:
 The
 interior
 spiritual life that flows into
 him through
 the ord
erly reception of goods
 and truths from
 the Divine,
 in
 each successive state of illumination, is
 progress
ively sanctified as
 to the will, cleansed as
 to the understanding, purified as to
 the interior thought, and washed as
 to the exterior life —
 freed
 from the fals
ity orig
inating in evil that
 had
 become
 intermingled with every
 good
 and
 truth he
 receives
.

**¶5:** The
 third: Such
 a person renders
 every act of the will into
 a form
 of good
.
 This
 is
 the hidden
 essence
 of those
 tru
ths born
 from wisdom, in
 whom there is no
 prof
anation —
 who
 neither
 viol
ate
 nor do
 violence to the goods and truths they
 receive.
 Rather
, they are set
 apart
;
 nothing
 of
 falsity or evil adh
eres to them,
 for
 they d
well in that
 heav
enly state
 in
 which
 goods and truths rest
 together
 without
 dist
urbance.

**¶6
:** The fourth: They take
 upon
 themselves the state
 of spiritual
 temptation,
 and they
 with
hold the power of their
 will from acting upon evil,
 so
 as not
 to ext
inguish the living affection of good
 and truth —
 the Divine life flowing
 within.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The first work: Shall the holy man punish his body by fasting, he subdues the entire ruling-power that exists in him.

The second: This soul that comes into him in the administration of his food, day by day; it shall be made holy, cleansed, purified, and washed from the adulteration of the Darkness that is mixed in with it.

The third: That person shall make every deed a holy one; the mystery of [the children] of light in whom there is neither corruption nor [defilement. They shall not harm] the food, nor wound it. Rather, they are holy, [there is nothing] in them that defiles, as they live in peace.
The fourth: They make a [seal upon] the Cross, they restrain their hands from the hand [of harm, and shall not] destroy the living soul.
